questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Opened.
questions.explanation: On a compressed gas tank, keep liquid discharge valves open during loading and unloading. Keep them closed at all other times.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and finish the trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Pull over safely and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over safely and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Stop and sleep if you feel drowsy while driving. Tired drivers cause many fatal accidents. Do not try to continue driving.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system allows poisonous fumes to enter your vehicle. Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Is probably aware of what is happening around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle and could do something dangerous.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking downhill.
Should never be used for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can release the brake air pressure and cause the brakes to fail. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ from any building.
questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, gathering place, or open fire.

questions.question: If hazardous cargo is leaking and you cannot reach a phone, you should:

options.text: Drive to find a phone and alert emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: If hazardous cargo leaks, stop driving to prevent more contamination. Park your vehicle, stay with it, and secure it. If you have no phone, send someone to get help.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: The speed of traffic around you.
Much slower than traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Match the speed of surrounding vehicles in heavy traffic. Vehicles moving at the same speed are less likely to crash. Never exceed legal speed limits.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is encouraged because:

options.text: The driver will have the best view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will have the best view.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's left side. This gives you the best view of the rear of your vehicle.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is usually more careful than a typical driver.
May be slower to make important decisions than a typical driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be slower to make important decisions than a typical driver.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers see and react to hazards more slowly than alert drivers. Drowsy driving impairs your ability to make critical decisions.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle can be:

options.text: Either awake or asleep inside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 100 feet of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A person attending a parked placarded vehicle must be either awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. If they are outside the vehicle, they must be able to see it clearly. They may not be in the sleeper berth.

questions.question: When backing up, follow a turning trailer by:

options.text: Doing nothing. The vehicle will naturally follow the trailer.
Changing the direction of the steering wheel.
Turning the steering wheel harder in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changing the direction of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel the opposite way of the turn. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: A person driving with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who likes fresh air.

questions.correctAnswerText: A distracted driver.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that another driver may be impaired. Drivers who have been drinking, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One sign of impairment is having windows rolled down in cold weather.

questions.question: While driving, gauges should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Watched for signs of trouble.
questions.explanation: Watch your vehicle's gauges while driving to spot any problems early. Check your gauges before starting your trip to make sure they work properly.

questions.question: Pushing in the trailer air supply control will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a minor truck fire, you should:

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: During a truck fire, feel the trailer doors before opening them. If they are hot, there may be a cargo fire. Keep the doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, such as at dawn or dusk, increase visibility by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using your vehicle's lights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights on low beam when driving at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather to make your vehicle more visible.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Use the mirrors on both sides of the truck when backing. Have someone help you whenever possible.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It distracts both your mind and hands.
People get too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts both your mind and hands.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it takes your mental focus away from driving and requires you to take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should include:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checking engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection of the engine, check the oil level, coolant level, and condition of the hoses.
